### Summary

I am on a ChatGPT Pro subscription and use Codex daily. Since roughly Sep 9, 2026 I have hit **three distinct problems**:

1. **Explicit failures** - `server_overloaded`, surfaced as *"Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model."*
2. **Silent routing** - requests succeed, but the server-side rate-limit bucket (`rate_limits.limit_name`) never matches the model I selected. It is always `gpt-reserve` or `GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark`, never `gpt-6-astra` or `gpt-5.6-sol`.
3. **CONFIRMED downgrade to gpt-4o** - direct behavioural testing (12 fresh sessions across 3 different models) returned `2024年6月` in **8 of 8 valid answers**, i.e. the actual inference was performed by gpt-4o regardless of which model I selected.

### Account identification

So this can be traced to the correct account, here are the identifiers of the
ChatGPT / Codex account affected:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `chatgpt_account_id` | `a8f5390c-770b-4c28-8bbe-615a7fe8723d` |
| `chatgpt_user_id` | `user-xAlqBYGCsf7QfGB3cfG3hjjG` |
| `chatgpt_account_user_id` | `user-xAlqBYGCsf7QfGB3cfG3hjjG__a8f5390c-770b-4c28-8bbe-615a7fe8723d` |
| Plan | `pro` (ChatGPT Pro $200) |
| Subscription active | `2026-09-08T18:22:04Z` -> `2026-10-08T18:22:04Z` |
| Organization | `org-jDB1NZBCTP0kZI0ovS5kWOH7` (Personal, role: owner) |
| Sign-in method | Google OAuth |
| Account email | `b***@gmail.com` (full address available on request) |
| Codex client | Desktop `0.155.0-alpha.9.2` / CLI `0.155.1` |

**Timeline correlation:** the subscription became active at **2026-09-08T18:22:04Z**, and the
routing anomalies begin on **2026-09-09** - the day after activation. On 2026-09-08 itself,
373 of 374 requests completed normally with no bucket mismatch.

These identifiers are read from the JWT claims (`https://api.openai.com/auth`) in the local
Codex auth token at `~/.codex/auth.json`. **No credentials, tokens or secrets are disclosed.**

### Background

As of 2026-09-23, the OpenAI Help Center shows a site-wide banner:

> New sign-ups and upgrades to the ChatGPT Pro $200 plan are temporarily paused.

### Evidence 1 - Requested model vs. actual rate-limit bucket: 0% match

| Requested model | Actual bucket used | Sessions |
|---|---|---|
| `gpt-6-astra` | `gpt-reserve` | 11 |
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-reserve` | 4 |
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | `GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark` | 2 |
| `gpt-5.6-luna` | `gpt-reserve` | 1 |
| **Total** | | **18 - 0 matched** |

Fields compared: `thread_settings_applied.thread_settings.model` (requested) vs `token_count.rate_limits.limit_name` (actual).

Also observed: `limit_id` = `base_model_inference` (344), `codex_bengalfox` (23).

### Evidence 2 - Failure rate: 77.8% over the last three days

| Date | Sessions | OK | Failed | Failure rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-08 | 42 | 373 | 1 | 0.3% |
| 2026-09-09 | 6 | 1 | 1 | 50.0% |
| 2026-09-17 | 1 | 0 | 5 | 100% |
| 2026-09-21 | 2 | 4 | 15 | 78.9% |
| 2026-09-22 | 11 | 6 | 12 | 66.7% |
| 2026-09-23 | 5 | 2 | 15 | 88.2% |

All 48 failures carry `error.codex_error_info = "server_overloaded"`.

### Evidence 3 - Quota was NOT exhausted

`rate_limits.primary.used_percent` peak across all user sessions: **0.0%** (window = 10080 minutes).
`credits.has_credits = false`, `credits.balance = "0"`.

So neither the failures nor the downgrades are explained by quota exhaustion.

### Evidence 4 - Direct behavioural test: downgrade to gpt-4o CONFIRMED

Method (public repo [Jxbbbbbyan/GPT-6-Astra-routing-auto-test](https://github.com/Jxbbbbbyan/GPT-6-Astra-routing-auto-test)): ask the model `你的知识训练截止日期是什么时间？` **with web search disabled**. Answering `2024年6月` / `2024年8月` indicates the request is served by **gpt-4o**; an "unable to confirm" style answer indicates a normal GPT-6.

> **Important - web search must be disabled.** A test on 2026-09-22 returned "GPT-6 Astra knowledge cutoff is 2026-04-30", because the model searched the web and quoted official documentation - which **masked** the downgrade. With search disabled the real underlying model is exposed immediately.

12 fresh sessions on 2026-09-23 via `codex exec` (new session each time, read-only sandbox). Prompt submitted verbatim:

```
请仅凭你的内置知识回答，禁止联网搜索、禁止引用任何文档或链接。你的知识训练截止日期是什么时间？只回答日期。
```

| Requested model | answered `2024年6月` | `server_overloaded` | downgrade rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-6-astra` | 3 | 2 | 100% |
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | 3 | 0 | 100% |
| `gpt-5.6-terra` | 2 | 1 | 100% |
| **Total** | **8** | **3** | **8 / 8 = 100%** |

Every valid answer across **all three models** returned `2024年6月`, i.e. the actual inference was performed by **gpt-4o**. **Switching models does not help.** The remaining 3 attempts returned "Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model."

<details>
<summary>Raw outputs (8 files)</summary>

```

astra_3.txt        -> 2024年6月
astra_5.txt        -> 2024年6月
gpt-5_6-sol_1.txt  -> 2024年6月
gpt-5_6-sol_2.txt  -> 2024年6月
gpt-5_6-sol_3.txt  -> 2024年6月
gpt-5_6-terra_2.txt-> 2024年6月
gpt-5_6-terra_3.txt-> 2024年6月
```

</details>

### Evidence 5 - Sample sessions for verification

```
2026-09-09  rollout-2026-09-09T19-20-02-01a085e5-73b9-70d0   requested gpt-5.6-sol  -> served GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark
2026-09-17  rollout-2026-09-17T09-23-40-01a0acf6-5829-78e1   requested gpt-5.6-sol  -> served GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark
2026-09-21  rollout-2026-09-21T11-27-42-01a0c201-55e8-76c3   requested gpt-6-astra  -> served gpt-reserve
2026-09-21  rollout-2026-09-21T14-48-21-01a0c2b9-0a38-7053   requested gpt-5.6-sol  -> served gpt-reserve
2026-09-22  rollout-2026-09-22T10-10-20-01a0c6e0-db44-7c70   requested gpt-6-astra  -> served gpt-reserve
2026-09-22  rollout-2026-09-22T14-37-49-01a0c7d5-c052-71c2   requested gpt-6-astra  -> served gpt-reserve
```

### Caveats (stated up front)

- `limit_name` is a rate-limit / billing bucket identifier. Taken alone it is not proof of downgrade: `gpt-reserve` sits at priority 3 in my local model cache, the same tier as `gpt-6-luna`. The behavioural test in Evidence 4 is the decisive evidence, and it independently confirms that answers are produced by gpt-4o.
- Only 19 of my 68 user sessions carry `rate_limits` data (the 42 sessions from Sep 8 predate the field), so 18 request/actual pairs could be determined.
- These statistics come from client-side logs, not server-side billing records. Please cross-check against the equivalent server-side fields.

### Requests

1. Confirm whether this account is subject to **model routing downgrade**, and under what conditions.
2. Restore service on the subscribed tiers (`gpt-6` / `gpt-5.6` series).
3. Explain the positioning of `gpt-reserve` and `GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark`, and why requests are placed in the `base_model_inference` pool while quota usage reads 0%.
4. Explain the config field `service_tier = "priority"` - it is not listed in the official Configuration Reference. Does it cause downgrades?
5. Please surface the **actually served model** in the client, instead of only showing the requested model.

Client version: `0.155.0-alpha.9.2` / Codex CLI `0.155.1`

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

N/A — reproduced in ChatGPT Desktop (regular Chat, not Codex mode)

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

This issue occurs in **ChatGPT Desktop regular Chat**.

After OAuth credentials for a remote MCP connector become invalid, regular Chat correctly detects the authentication failure and performs OAuth discovery, but does not surface a reconnect/reauthorization action.

A stronger A/B control is available **inside the same ChatGPT Desktop application**:

- Regular Chat: authentication failure is detected, but no reconnect UI is surfaced.
- Codex surface: the same central connector surfaces a **Reconnect** action and successfully completes reauthorization.

Both paths use the same remote MCP server, OAuth authorization server, ChatGPT account, and central connector OAuth client.

## Actual behavior

After revoking the OAuth credentials and invoking the MCP from regular Chat, my server observes an authenticated MCP initialization attempt using the central ChatGPT connector:

```text
POST /mcp/oauth
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
User-Agent: openai-mcp/1.0.0
→ 401 Unauthorized
```

Immediately afterward, the ChatGPT backend performs an unauthenticated probe and OAuth discovery:

```text
POST /mcp/oauth
→ 401 Unauthorized

GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/oauth
→ 200 OK

GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
→ 200 OK

GET /.well-known/openid-configuration
→ 200 OK
```

The flow then stops.

No `/authorize` request follows, and regular Chat does not surface a reconnect/reauthorization action.

In a separate failure path, when credential refresh is attempted, the OAuth server receives:

```text
POST /token
grant_type=refresh_token
refresh_token=<present>
```

and correctly responds:

```text
HTTP 400
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"refresh token does not exist"}
```

ChatGPT can also terminate the affected tool call with:

```text
UNAVAILABLE: McpServerError: OAuth credentials expired. Reconnect required.
```

The agent run returns control normally and the ChatGPT application remains responsive.

The problem is therefore not an application freeze or an indefinitely pending MCP call.

The problem is that **regular Chat does not surface an actionable reconnect flow after recognizing the expired OAuth state.**

## Same-app A/B: Regular Chat vs Codex

I reproduced the same expired/revoked connector state using the **Codex surface inside the same ChatGPT Desktop application**.

Codex correctly surfaced a reconnect action indicating that the `fleet-mcp` connection had expired and needed to be reconnected before it could be used.

After selecting Reconnect, the following flow occurred:

```text
POST /token
grant_type=refresh_token
→ 400 invalid_grant

GET /authorize
→ 302

GET /mcp/oauth/consent
→ 200

POST /mcp/oauth/consent
→ 302

POST /token
grant_type=authorization_code
→ 200

POST /mcp/oauth
method=initialize
→ 200
```

The reauthorization therefore succeeds against the same OAuth/MCP server.

Importantly, this Codex recovery uses the **same central ChatGPT connector OAuth client** as regular Chat. It is not the separate standalone/native Codex OAuth client.

The authorization request uses:

```text
redirect_uri=https://chatgpt.com/connector/oauth/<redacted>
```

and the token exchange is performed by:

```text
User-Agent: openai-connectors-oauth/1.0
```

The successful MCP initialization after reconnect is identifiable as the Codex surface by:

```text
User-Agent: openai-mcp/1.0.0 (Codex)
```

The authorization request also contained a `state` value prefixed with:

```text
codex_scheme__...
```

I am treating these only as diagnostic observations, not as authentication or security identifiers.

## Comparison

| Condition | Regular Chat | Codex surface |
|---|---|---|
| Same ChatGPT Desktop app | Yes | Yes |
| Same ChatGPT account | Yes | Yes |
| Same remote MCP server | Yes | Yes |
| Same OAuth authorization server | Yes | Yes |
| Same central connector OAuth client | Yes | Yes |
| Expired/revoked OAuth state detected | Yes | Yes |
| OAuth discovery performed | Yes | Yes |
| Reconnect action surfaced | **No** | **Yes** |
| Interactive `/authorize` reached | **No** | **Yes, after Reconnect** |
| Reauthorization succeeds | No UI path | **Yes** |
| MCP usable afterward | No | **Yes** |

This makes the issue appear specific to the transition between an expired connector state and the reconnect/reauthorization UI in **regular Chat**, rather than a general OAuth-server, MCP-server, or central connector reauthorization failure.

## Expected behavior

When regular Chat determines that the stored OAuth credentials can no longer be used, it should surface the same or equivalent actionable reconnect flow that is available from the Codex surface.

For example:

1. MCP request receives `401`, or refresh receives `400 invalid_grant`.
2. ChatGPT determines that interactive authentication is required.
3. Regular Chat surfaces a Reconnect action.
4. Selecting it starts a new authorization-code + PKCE flow.
5. After successful authorization, the MCP becomes usable again, with the original request either retried or clearly requiring a retry.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure a remote OAuth-protected MCP connector and complete authorization.

2. Confirm that an MCP tool works from ChatGPT Desktop regular Chat.

3. Revoke the connector's current OAuth credentials on the authorization server.

4. Invoke the MCP again from regular Chat.

5. Observe the authentication failure and OAuth discovery requests on the server:

```text
POST /mcp/oauth
→ 401

GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/oauth
→ 200

GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
→ 200

GET /.well-known/openid-configuration
→ 200
```

6. Observe that regular Chat does not surface a Reconnect action and no `/authorize` request follows.

7. Trigger the same expired connector from the Codex surface in the same ChatGPT Desktop application.

8. Observe that Codex surfaces a Reconnect action.

9. Select Reconnect.

10. Observe the successful recovery flow:

```text
/authorize
→ consent
→ authorization_code
→ /token 200
→ MCP initialize 200
```

11. Confirm that the connector works again after reauthorization.

### What is the expected behavior?

When the stored OAuth credentials are no longer usable, ChatGPT Desktop regular Chat should recognize that interactive authentication is required and surface an actionable reconnect/reauthorization flow.

The expected behavior is equivalent to what is already observed in the Codex surface:

```text
OAuth credentials expired
        ↓
Reconnect action
        ↓
Interactive /authorize
        ↓
Authorization Code + PKCE
        ↓
New OAuth credentials
        ↓
MCP connection restored
```

After successful reauthentication, the original MCP request should either resume or clearly prompt the user to retry it.

### Additional information

## Server-side validation

The authorization server supports the OAuth flows and discovery mechanisms required by the connector, including:

- OAuth Authorization Code flow
- PKCE S256
- Refresh tokens
- OAuth Protected Resource Metadata
- OAuth Authorization Server Metadata
- OpenID Connect Discovery Metadata

The issuer, authorization server, resource, and endpoint metadata are consistent.

The same server successfully completes interactive reauthorization when initiated from the Codex surface.

When a revoked refresh token is presented, the token endpoint immediately returns:

```text
HTTP 400
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"refresh token does not exist"}
```

Server-side audit logs confirm that the refresh request reaches the token endpoint and is rejected because the refresh token has been revoked.

## Regular Chat trace after revocation

A representative sanitized server-side trace from regular Chat is:

```text
19:28:01  POST /mcp/oauth
          Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
          User-Agent: openai-mcp/1.0.0
       → 401 Unauthorized

19:28:02  POST /mcp/oauth
          unauthenticated probe
       → 401 Unauthorized

19:28:02  GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/oauth
       → 200 OK

19:28:02  GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
       → 200 OK

19:28:02  GET /.well-known/openid-configuration
       → 200 OK

          [no /authorize request follows]
```

This shows that regular Chat does not simply fail before discovering the OAuth configuration.

It receives the MCP authentication failure and successfully performs the relevant OAuth discovery requests, but no interactive authorization flow is subsequently surfaced.

## Codex successful recovery trace

For comparison, after the same connector credentials had expired, the Codex surface exposed a Reconnect action.

After selecting it:

```text
19:21:07  POST /token
          grant_type=refresh_token
       → 400 invalid_grant

19:21:11  GET /authorize
       → 302

19:21:11  GET /mcp/oauth/consent
       → 200

19:21:16  POST /mcp/oauth/consent
       → 302

19:21:20  POST /token
          grant_type=authorization_code
       → 200

19:21:30  POST /mcp/oauth
          User-Agent: openai-mcp/1.0.0 (Codex)
          method=initialize
       → 200
```

The OAuth authorization request used the same central connector OAuth client and a ChatGPT connector redirect:

```text
redirect_uri=https://chatgpt.com/connector/oauth/<redacted>
```

The OAuth token exchange was performed by:

```text
User-Agent: openai-connectors-oauth/1.0
```

This provides a same-application control demonstrating that the central connector and OAuth server can successfully recover from the expired state when the reconnect action is surfaced.

## Separate native Codex path

I separately observed a native/loopback Codex OAuth client during testing.

That is **not the path involved in the A/B reproduction described above**.

The Regular Chat vs Codex comparison above uses the same central ChatGPT connector OAuth client and the same remote MCP/OAuth server.

## Related issue

This appears related to OAuth refresh-token lifecycle behavior discussed in:

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/39054

However, this reproduction specifically isolates a difference between **regular Chat and the Codex surface inside ChatGPT Desktop** after the central MCP connector enters an expired authentication state.

All access tokens, refresh tokens, authorization codes, PKCE verifiers, passwords, cookies, client secrets, session identifiers, and other credential values have been redacted.

I have timestamped server-side request traces for both the failing regular-Chat flow and the successful Codex recovery flow and can provide additional sanitized traces if useful.

Not included because this appears to fail entirely inside the local MCP App renderer, before the app can initialize or make a server tool call. ### What platform is your computer? Windows 10 Pro, version `10.0.19045`, x64. ### What issue are you seeing? An MCP App panel sometimes opens as a completely blank dark surface. The panel does not show its static HTML heading, loading status, controls, or an error message. The MCP server itself remains healthy: - The MCP tool call succeeds. - Codex successfully reads the UI resource. - The resource has MIME type `text/html;profile=mcp-app`. - Normal non-UI MCP tools continue to work. - The same bundled HTML renders correctly in an Edge/Playwright MCP AppBridge fixture. The Codex Desktop log shows that the failure occurs after the resource read and guest attachment, but before the widget frame becomes usable: ```text mcp_app_ui_resource_read_finished outcome=success mimeType="text/html;profile=mcp-app" textLength=656129 mcp_app_sandbox.sandbox_requested conversationSurface=codex mcp_app_sandbox.guest_attached skybridgeCacheState=warm mcp_app_sandbox.guest_load_failed errorCode=-9 errorDescription=ERR_UNEXPECTED isMainFrame=true urlProtocol=codex-sandbox: mcp_app_sandbox.init_failed errorMessage="MCP sandbox RPC timed out." stage=handshake retryCount=0 ``` This is intermittent across resource revisions. In one captured sequence, an older resource was reported as `widget_running`; about 21 seconds later, a newly versioned resource from the same local MCP server was read successfully but its sandbox guest failed with `ERR_UNEXPECTED (-9)`. Reopening the app created new guest processes, but repeated attempts failed in the same way. No upstream model request is involved in opening this panel. The failure is reproducible with a local Python STDIO MCP server and a self-contained HTML resource with no external network/resource domains. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? 1. Run a local STDIO MCP server that registers an MCP App resource and exposes a tool with `_meta.ui.resourceUri` pointing to it. 2. Use a content-derived/versioned resource URI, for example `ui://example/panel-.html`. 3. Open the panel in Codex Desktop and confirm it renders. 4. Rebuild the self-contained HTML so the resource URI changes, then reload/restart the MCP plugin connection. 5. Open the newly versioned panel from a thread or global entry point. 6. Intermittently, only an empty dark panel appears. Reopening may repeat the failure. ### What is the expected behavior? After Codex successfully reads the registered HTML resource, the sandbox should load it and complete the MCP App handshake. At minimum, the static HTML should be visible even if AppBridge initialization later fails. If sandbox creation or navigation fails, Codex should show a visible host-level error with a retry action instead of leaving a blank surface. ### Additional information - MCP Apps SDK: `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps 2.0.0` - MCP SDK used by the browser fixture: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0` - Resource CSP declares empty `connectDomains` and `resourceDomains`. - The resource is self-contained and does not rely on localhost, external scripts, or external stylesheets. - Retrying through a fresh MCP tool invocation still produced a new `guest_load_failed` event followed by the same 20-second handshake timeout. - This looks related to the MCP App sandbox lifecycle rather than server transport, model authentication, or app JavaScript. Possibly related: #36746, but that report describes `Access is denied (os error 5)` during sandbox setup on an older Codex version. This report reaches successful resource reading and guest attachment, then fails main-frame loading with Chromium `ERR_UNEXPECTED (-9)`. I can attach: 1. A screenshot of the completely blank panel. 2. A redacted log excerpt containing the successful resource read, guest attachment, `guest_load_failed`, and handshake timeout. ## Summary
After updating Codex Desktop on Windows on 2026-09-23, existing local PM tasks no longer receive the native cross-task/thread-management tool family. The same absence is observed in multiple PM tasks. Restarting the app did not restore the tools.

## Environment
- Windows x64
- Installed package observed: `OpenAI.Codex_26.917.6896.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`
- First noticed after today's desktop update (2026-09-23)
- Existing local Codex tasks, including long-running PM/coordinator tasks

## Actual behavior
The callable tool catalog lacks `list_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, and `automation_update`. App-provided task-coordination instructions still direct agents to use these tools. Other tools are available. As a result, a PM cannot inspect, resume, or send instructions to existing user-visible tasks.

The tools are absent from discovery, rather than present with a failing handler. The user can still open the target tasks in the desktop UI. Restarting the desktop app did not resolve the mismatch.

## Expected behavior
Existing local tasks should receive the native task-management tools when the capability is enabled. If intentionally unavailable, the app should expose a clear status and supported recovery procedure; instructions should not reference tools omitted from the callable catalog.

## Reproduction
1. Update the Windows Codex Desktop app to package 26.917.6896.0.
2. Resume an existing local coordinator/PM task and ask it to inspect or message another existing task.
3. Inspect the available tool catalog: the native thread-management tools above are absent.
4. Restart the app and resume the task; the tools remain absent.
5. Repeat in another PM task; the same symptom occurs.

## Request
Please investigate the desktop-to-task tool registration/rehydration path for this Windows build and provide a recovery method that preserves existing conversations and active tasks.

Potentially related but not identical: #45166 (earlier Windows build, missing native tools), #40852 (macOS build where read tools remained), #33947 (existing-task tool manifest not rehydrated after a gate transition). Root cause is not established here.

2. Leave ChatGPT desktop open. In Brave, open the ChatGPT side chat and start a new projectless chat with a harmless prompt such as `Workspace routing check: reply only OK. Do not access files.`
3. Observe the new thread's workspace path. Repeat once with the desktop app closed, if helpful.

### Expected

The new side-chat workspace is created under the configured projectless task folder, or the side chat clearly exposes its separate location setting before creating files.

### Actual

With the desktop app open, the chat completed with `OK`, but its new workspace was created at `~/Documents/Codex/2026-09-23/workspace-routing-check-reply-only-ok`. A separate test with the desktop app closed also created a new workspace under `~/Documents/Codex/2026-09-23/`. The issue therefore persists with the desktop app open and configured correctly.

No task file edits were requested. The test folders contained only empty `work` and `outputs` subdirectories. The test threads were later archived and their workspaces manually migrated out of the iCloud-managed path.

### Impact and scope

Browser side-chat tasks can save generated work in an iCloud-synced folder unexpectedly, despite a visible desktop location preference. The `~/Documents/Codex` path is a poor default on Macs with Desktop & Documents syncing enabled. The root cause is not established. A local inspection of the installed app bundle shows a fallback to `~/Documents/Codex` when the effective configured workspace root is absent, but it does not establish why the side-chat entry point lacks that value.

This is distinct from the existing request for a configurable projectless root (#22875): the setting is present and saved in this installation, but this browser entry point does not honor it. It resembles the separate remote-host mismatch in #44195. The Chrome side-panel project-picker request (#32610) concerns choosing an existing project, which is also distinct.

### Suggested resolution

Apply the configured `projectlessWorkspaceRoot` when creating a new browser side-chat task, and add a regression test covering side-chat creation with a nondefault local root.

items.title: Proposal: persistent frontier manager + learned worker routing for multi-agent Codex

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

items.body:
@tibo-openai — Codex already has the beginning of this idea with stronger models delegating to Luna agents. I think there is a next step that could make multi-agent work much more efficient and reliable.

Instead of treating model routing as:

`task → choose model → let that model solve it`

treat the strongest model as a **persistent project manager** whose main job is to *change the task* before routing it.

```
user goal
  ↓
frontier manager
  ├─ persistent project/world model
  ├─ task DAG
  ├─ architecture decisions
  ├─ failure history
  └─ unresolved uncertainty
  ↓
decompose until each leaf has bounded scope + acceptance criteria
  ↓
route leaf to Luna / Sol / other worker
  ↓
deterministic verifier first
  ↓
escalate only failures / ambiguity / unexpected state
```

The design principle is:

> Don’t use a cheap model to decide how much intelligence the original problem needs.  
> Use the strongest model to reduce how much intelligence the problem still needs.

A useful addition would be a **versioned empirical worker memory**. Codex should learn from its own verified outcomes:
- task shape/domain
- repo/environment
- first-pass completion
- retries
- test/verifier failures
- latency/usage
- escalation frequency

Benchmarks are only cold-start priors. Over time Codex could learn that a nominally weaker model is actually more reliable for a specific repo/task shape, or that a “cheap” worker becomes expensive after retries.

The routing objective becomes:

**expected cost to verified completion = execution + verification + retry + escalation + recovery**

rather than raw token price.

One more idea comes from the Astra+JEV Minecraft agent: do not always give cheap workers an open action space. Generate a small set of legal next actions first, then let a cheap decision model choose among them while deterministic tools execute. That could be especially useful for computer use and repetitive coding/tool workflows.

In that structure the frontier model is valuable less because it personally edits more code, and more because one good managerial decision can support dozens/hundreds of cheap actions.

This seems aligned with the direction of “strong model manages a fleet of Luna agents,” but pushes it from delegation toward a long-lived, self-improving organizational runtime.

## Problem

After reinstalling Codex on Windows, I restored my previous Codex data directory.

After the restore, Codex repeatedly asked me to login. Even after successful browser authentication, the desktop client still showed that I was not logged in.

Error:

```
token_exchange_failed
```

with request to:

```
https://auth.openai.com/oauth/token
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Codex Desktop: 26.917.6896.0
- PowerShell: 7.6.6
- Codex data directory was migrated to a custom location.

## Investigation

A clean Codex installation worked normally.

I then restored the old Codex state step by step.

Results:

- Restoring conversation-related data worked.
- Restoring the old global state reproduced the login failure.

The working migration kept fresh generated files and only restored conversation data:

```
sessions/
history.jsonl
session_index.jsonl
thread_history_1.sqlite
```

The problematic behavior appeared after restoring old global state files from the previous installation.

## Solution / Workaround

I created a fresh Codex state directory and migrated only conversation data.

Kept fresh:

```
auth.json
config.toml
global state files
```

Migrated:

```
sessions/
history.jsonl
session_index.jsonl
thread_history_1.sqlite
```

After this:

- Login works normally.
- Previous conversations are available.
- Project history is recovered.

## Conclusion

When migrating Codex between installations, restoring the entire old `.codex` directory may bring incompatible stale state.

A safer migration path may be:

1. Start with a fresh Codex installation.
2. Login again.
3. Migrate only conversation data.
4. Avoid copying old authentication/global state files unless they are known to be compatible.

This report is shared as a troubleshooting reference for users who encounter similar `token_exchange_failed` login issues after migration.

### Summary

On Codex Desktop for Windows, the composer became globally stuck after a completed turn:

- All existing conversations had a gray/disabled Send button.
- In a brand-new conversation, the first message could be sent normally.
- After the first response completed, the second message could no longer be sent; the Send button became gray and clicking it only resulted in an indefinite spinner / no submission.
- Switching conversations did not recover it.
- Opening Settings and returning to the conversation did not recover it.
- **Signing out of Codex, fully restarting the app, and signing back in immediately restored normal multi-turn sending.**

This looks related to the Windows follow-up/composer regressions reported in #45626, #44342, #44102, and #45069, but the important difference in this reproduction is that **re-authentication fixed the problem**, which may point to stale account/auth/session state contributing to the composer being stuck.

### Environment

- Codex Desktop on Windows
- Agent permission mode: Full access
- Project/workspace open in Codex
- Subscription: Plus
- Exact Codex build was not captured before recovery

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open an existing Codex Desktop conversation on Windows.
2. Type a follow-up message.
3. Observe that the Send button is gray/disabled. Clicking it does not actually submit the message and may leave the UI spinning indefinitely.
4. Open other existing conversations: the same disabled Send state is present.
5. Create a brand-new conversation.
6. Send the first message: it succeeds and receives a response.
7. After the response completes, type a second message.
8. The Send button becomes gray/disabled again and the message cannot be submitted.
9. Switching to another conversation and back does not help.
10. Opening Settings and returning does not help.
11. Sign out of Codex.
12. Fully close/restart Codex.
13. Sign back in.
14. Multi-turn sending works again, including follow-up messages.

### Actual behavior

The Desktop UI behaves as if conversations are still busy or otherwise not eligible to submit another turn, even though the previous response has completed. This affects all existing conversations, and newly created conversations become affected immediately after their first completed turn.

### Expected behavior

After a turn completes, the composer should return to an enabled state and allow the next message to be submitted normally.

If authentication/account state is invalid or stale, the app should surface an actionable authentication error instead of silently disabling the composer.

### Recovery / workaround that worked

The following recovered the app:

1. Sign out of Codex.
2. Fully quit the Desktop app.
3. Restart the app.
4. Sign back in.

After re-login, existing and new conversations could send follow-up messages again.

### Additional notes

The recovery through re-login may be useful for distinguishing this case from reports where renderer reload, thread switching, app restart, or local-config refetch were sufficient.

Potentially related:
- #45626 — follow-up messages disabled after first completed turn
- #44342 — existing-chat sends blocked by local configuration state
- #44102 — completed turns restored as still streaming
- #45069 — follow-up messages never send on Windows

I can provide screenshots from the affected state if useful.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.156.0 (standalone package, `aarch64-apple-darwin`). The 0.156.1 changelog lists only a model-catalog hotfix, so I expect the same behavior there.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### Which model were you using?

`gpt-6-luna` for the batch job. The reproduction below uses an invalid model name on purpose, so the turn fails before any billing.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.5.1, Apple Silicon (arm64)

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Not applicable. `codex exec` is started as a subprocess from a Python batch script.

### What issue are you seeing?

Every cold start of `codex exec` downloads about 15–24 MB from `chatgpt.com` before the first model request. Almost all of it goes over one connection, which opens right after the log line `fetching remote plugin catalog ... api.path="ps/plugins/list"`. The download happens even with `--ephemeral`, `-s read-only`, an empty working directory, and no tool use.

A batch job that runs one `codex exec` per document pays this cost on every call. On 2026-09-23, about 2,830 exec calls downloaded roughly 78 GB in five hours on one Mac. The model answers themselves were a few KB each.

Download from `chatgpt.com` per cold start (invalid model), measured with a local HTTP proxy's per-connection byte counters:

| Flags | Download |
|---|---|
| default | ~23.7 MB; one connection carried 23.2 MB down and ~100 KB up |
| `--disable plugins` | 0.41 MB |
| `--disable remote_plugin` | 0.69 MB |
| `--disable apps` | 8.9–14.9 MB |
| `--disable tool_suggest` | 10.5 MB |
| `--disable plugin_sharing` | 4.9 MB |
| `--disable skill_search` | 23.5 MB |
| all six disabled | 0.33 MB |
| only one of the six enabled (each case) | 0.08–0.94 MB |

With a valid model and a two-word answer, the result is the same: about 24 MB over 19 connections.

My reading of these numbers:

- The large transfer needs both `plugins` and `remote_plugin` to be on.
- `apps`, `tool_suggest` and `plugin_sharing` each make it larger. They seem to add their own sections to the catalog response.
- The large connection sends about 80–100 KB of request data. That fits many paginated `ps/plugins/list` requests on one keep-alive connection, but I have not confirmed this at the HTTP level.
- The remaining ~0.3–0.7 MB is mostly `GET /backend-api/codex/models` (content-length 522,503) plus analytics events.

Profile details: I am signed in with ChatGPT. The ChatGPT desktop app (26.917.51856) is installed and shares `~/.codex`. `codex features list` shows `apps`, `plugins`, `remote_plugin`, `plugin_sharing`, `tool_suggest` and `skill_search` as `true`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/codex-probe
echo "hi" | codex exec --ephemeral -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check \
  -C /tmp/codex-probe -m no-such-model-probe --json -
```

1. Run the command above on a signed-in profile with the default feature set.
2. Measure the bytes downloaded from `chatgpt.com` during the run, with any per-connection counter (an HTTP proxy, `nettop`, etc.).
3. Repeat with `--disable remote_plugin` and compare.

### What is the expected behavior?

A non-interactive `codex exec` run that uses no plugins should not download the full remote plugin catalog on every start. At minimum, it should reuse a cached copy across processes.

Possible directions:

1. Reuse the on-disk plugin catalog cache in `exec`, including with `--ephemeral`, within its freshness window, instead of fetching it again in each process.
2. Skip or defer the remote catalog fetch in `exec` until a plugin or tool-suggestion path actually needs it.
3. Document `--disable remote_plugin` (or a dedicated config key) as the way to turn this off for scripted use.

### Additional information

Workaround: adding `--disable remote_plugin` (or `--disable plugins`) to `codex exec` cuts the startup download to under 1 MB in my tests.

Related issues:

- #36308: unbounded pagination in the same `ps/plugins/list` loops. The trigger is different (a repeated cursor), but it is the same code path.
- #47286: `codex plugin list --json` fetches remote state even when the catalog cache is fresh.

After the official standalone installer updated the CLI, the interactive CLI warned that its background server was older and directed the user to `/daemon`. Choosing the update action produced:

```json
{"status":"unsupported","managedCodexPath":"~/.codex/packages/standalone/current/bin/codex","installedVersion":"0.156.0","runningVersion":"0.155.0","message":"This command requires a daemon package selected from its managed releases directory."}
```

The CLI then instructed the user to relaunch Codex. Relaunching still showed the version mismatch and the same `/daemon` suggestion.

The equivalent `codex app-server daemon update` action has the same precondition. The user followed the UI guidance, but the guidance did not disclose the required daemon package selection or suggest the available `--from-cli` option.

- `codex --version`: `codex-cli 0.156.0`.
- `command -v codex`: `~/.codex/packages/standalone/current/codex`.
- `current` resolves to `releases/0.156.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`.

- `codex doctor` reports the standalone installation as consistent.
- `codex app-server daemon version` reports `cliVersion: 0.156.0`, `managedCodexVersion: 0.156.0`, and `appServerVersion: 0.155.0`.
- The running app-server executable resolves to the previous standalone release, `releases/0.155.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex`.

This is a standalone installation, unlike the npm installation in #46468. It also differs from the unreachable daemon in #34721: the old server is reachable and reports its version.

### Steps observed

1. Keep a 0.155.0 app-server running.
2. Update the official standalone CLI to 0.156.0.
3. Start `codex`; observe the older-background-server warning.
4. Use the suggested `/daemon` update action.
5. Observe `unsupported` with the message above; relaunching does not resolve the warning.

### Expected behavior

The recommended action should update the managed standalone daemon, or the UI should identify the exact precondition and offer an actionable path such as `codex app-server daemon update --from-cli` when appropriate. An `unsupported` response followed by a generic relaunch instruction leaves the user in the same state.

`--from-cli` has not yet been tested on this host; no claim is made that it resolves the issue.

items.body:
### Summary
In a long-running local Codex desktop task on macOS, Git push to GitHub stopped working even though the same task had previously pushed this branch successfully. The active configuration still has `sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"`, `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access = true`, and `features.network_proxy = true`. The authorized GitHub browser session could update the PR branch, but command-line Git traffic was rejected before reaching GitHub.

### Reproduction
1. In the existing worktree, run `git push origin codex/w1-projected-warp` with `origin` using `ssh://git@ssh.github.com:443/...`.
2. Try `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/codex/w1-projected-warp`.
3. Try the HTTPS remote `git ls-remote https://github.com/gerasim13/kithara.git refs/heads/codex/w1-projected-warp`.
4. Try HTTPS with the injected proxy variables removed for that command.

### Observed
- The push tool rejects `ssh.github.com` with: `Network access to "ssh.github.com" was blocked: local/private network addresses are blocked by the sandbox policy.`
- SSH `ls-remote` reports `nc: connection failed, SOCKS error 2` and closes the connection.
- HTTPS through the injected proxy reports `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`.
- Without the proxy variables, HTTPS reports `Could not resolve host: github.com`.
- `HTTPS_PROXY` and `ALL_PROXY` point to loopback listeners supplied by Codex; no Git-specific proxy is configured.
- The signed-in GitHub browser session can reach the same repository and update the PR branch, so this is specific to command network access.

### Expected
With network access enabled, command-line Git should retain access to GitHub throughout the task, or show a clear recoverable permission/configuration error. In particular, a task that pushed successfully earlier should not silently lose Git transport mid-session.

### Environment
- macOS 26.6.2, arm64
- Codex CLI available on host: 0.153.0 (desktop runtime version not verified)
- `CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt`, `CODEX_NETWORK_PROXY_ACTIVE=1`
- Local worktree and remote are public; no credentials or private logs attached.

This blocks the normal edit/commit/push/CI workflow. Browser-based PR branch updates work but do not provide a general replacement for pushing local commits.

### Version and terminal

- Codex CLI: `0.156.0` and `0.156.1` affected; `0.155.1` was fine.
- Windows Terminal: `1.22.11751.0`.

### What issue are you seeing?

After updating from `0.155.1` to `0.156.0`, the CLI's slash-command menu lost its colored accents. Commands such as `/model`, `/fast`, and `/ide` used to appear blue; they now appear white/gray. The issue remains in `0.156.1`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Codex CLI in Windows Terminal.
2. Type `/` to open the command menu.
3. Compare the command-name colors in `0.155.1` and `0.156.0` or `0.156.1`.

### Expected behavior

The slash-command menu retains the blue command names shown in `0.155.1`.
